what_this_proves: The documents family is no longer structurally read-only. A file is written, appended to, edited, renamed, moved, copied or sent to the Recycle Bin only through a journaled mutation: the device backs the file up to its own undo store first, writes atomically, and answers the record before and after with sha256; the Cloud Core records every change as a file_mutations row (the version history, the approval queue, the receipt), applies the risky ones only after the owner's word through the same read-back + confirmation gate mail drafts use, and undoes any applied change by running its inverse plan and reading the result back. One host flag closes the whole surface. Nothing deletes permanently.

measured_first.cloud_before: No write/append/rename/move/copy/delete tool in tools_documents (ADR-0083 decision 7); the corpus case doc.neg.delete proved 'Bu dosyayı sil.' reached nothing; DocumentCapabilityNames.All = 8; no undo journal, no mutation receipt, no hash-before/after, no approval surface for files; documents_mutation_enabled did not exist.
measured_first.router_before: 'Bu dosyada X yerine Y yaz' → type_text (the operator's typing took it); 'Bu dosyanın sonuna ... ekle' → calendar_propose ('... ekle' with a meeting word); 'Bu dosyayı kopyala' → none; 'Uygula.' → none; 'Bu dosyayı sil' → none. Measured 2026-09-15 before the matchers were written.
measured_first.relay: the realtime relay refuses a tool argument named 'text' (FORBIDDEN_KEY_PARTS treats it as transcript-shaped); the mutation tools take 'content'.
measured_first.device_probe: the documents lab's fixture copy is the only authorised root, so a bucket name (documents/desktop) resolves outside it there and is refused by the same confinement the real desktop applies; the lab tests use absolute paths inside the lab root and the cloud tests use the fake's bucket prefixes.

closed_fully.153_167_edit: document.edit: 'Bu dosyada X yerine Y yaz' → the file's current text through file.read (64 KiB pages), the words replaced the way the owner SAID them (Turkish casefold, and without diacritics when ASR dropped them), a PROPOSAL row (sensitive) with the plan {file.write, expected_sha256 = the hash it read}; nothing written until 'Uygula.'; a word not in the file is text_not_found, never a guess.
closed_fully.154_write: document.write: 'X adında bir dosya oluştur' + the model's content → a NEW text file in Belgeler (or the spoken folder, as a bucket the device resolves); low risk, applied at once, journaled, undo = Recycle Bin with a backup.
closed_fully.155_append: document.append: 'Bu dosyanın sonuna ... ekle' → file.append with expected_sha256; low risk, applied at once, backup kept, undo = file.restore.
closed_fully.156_rename: document.rename: 'Bu dosyanın adını X yap' → proposal → file.rename (the extension kept when none was said); undo renames back.
closed_fully.157_move: document.move: 'Bu dosyayı Masaüstüne taşı' → proposal (critical) → file.move {destination_folder: bucket}; undo moves back to the folder of path_before.
closed_fully.158_copy: document.copy: 'Bu dosyayı kopyala / ... X adıyla kopyala / ... Masaüstüne kopyala' → proposal → file.copy (never over an existing file; '<name> - kopya.<ext>' when nothing was said); undo trashes the copy with a backup.
closed_fully.159_161_delete: document.delete: 'Bu dosyayı sil' / 'çöp kutusuna gönder' → proposal (critical) → file.trash {backup: true}: the Recycle Bin, a copy in the undo store first; undo = file.restore. Permanent deletion is offered by nothing (the shape of that policy is the owner's checkpoint).
closed_fully.160_undo: document.undo: the last applied row's inverse plan (derived from the device's ANSWER, never from the request) run on the device and read back; the original row becomes undone and the restore is a row of its own (undo_of); nothing to undo is refused by name.
closed_fully.162_163_receipt_hashes: every receipt is composed from the row: sha_before/sha_after/backup_id/path_after in the receipt and the ledger event; a device answer without an 'after' record carrying a hash (or, for a delete, observed.exists false) is recorded failed, never verified.
closed_fully.164_versions: document.versions: the journal rows for the file's path, newest first, spoken with time and kind; the REST journal lists them all.
closed_fully.165_atomic: device: FileMutations.WriteAtomic - a temporary file beside the target and one rename over it; a BOM the file had is kept; the artifacts family's atomic write is now matched on the documents side.
closed_fully.166_approval: risk_of: write-new/append low (applied at once), overwrite/edit/rename/copy sensitive, move/delete critical; sensitive and critical are proposals read back to the session (read_back_at/read_back_session_id/read_back_turn) and applied only by 'Uygula.'/'Kaydet.' (the router resolves DOCUMENT_APPLY only while a change is pending for THIS session, and the tool's owner_intent_ok is the router's verdict) or the Cockpit's confirm; another session's 'Uygula.' is not_read_back; a second 'Uygula.' is nothing_pending.
closed_fully.674_permission: settings.documents_mutation_enabled (default True) closes the whole surface with one flag (mutation_disabled); the device's authorised roots, secret-name refusal and text-like-only rule stand under it; step-up tiers: write/append/apply/undo CRITICAL, the proposals SENSITIVE.
closed_fully.device: DocumentCapabilityNames.All 8 → 14: file.write / file.append / file.rename / file.move / file.copy / file.restore (+ file.trash {backup}); FileMutations.cs (backup store <root>\.pagentos-undo with sidecars, newest 500 kept, hidden, skipped by file.search; text-like kinds only for write/append; every answer before/after/backup/observed); DocumentCapabilities dispatch with the family's own confinement (ResolveTarget for existing files, ConfineNewFile for a path that does not exist yet, ConfineFolderEntry for a bucket); DEVICE_PROTOCOL.md §6 rows.
closed_fully.rest_and_cockpit: GET /v1/documents/mutations (journal), GET /pending (lists = read-back for the owner session), POST /{id}/confirm|discard|undo through the same MutationService and the same device port the voice tools use; the Cockpit's Documents panel lists pending changes with the sentence the owner heard, the hash of what is there, and the same Onayla/Vazgeç pair drafts and proposals use (approvals.ts + useApprovalPair mutations family; the twenty-eighth quiet family).
closed_fully.router: Intent.DOCUMENT_WRITE/APPEND/EDIT/RENAME/MOVE/COPY/DELETE/APPLY/UNDO/VERSIONS; the block sits before the operator's typing matcher (which owned 'X yerine Y yaz') and before M21's confirmations; names are read off the RAW text (the tokenizer cuts 'notlar-yeni.md' into pieces); other families' nouns (mail, calendar, alarm, duplicates, native, artifacts) are refused in the TARGET part of the sentence; the bare 'Vazgeç.' targets document.discard when a file change is the only thing pending.

red_first_proof.method: Executed mutations restored from sha256-verified copies (never git checkout); the C# mutations rebuild the agent tests and run the lab suite, then the restored tree is rebuilt.
mutations: M1 document.apply skips the read-back/confirmation gate -> 1 failure (another session's 'Uygula.' applied).
M2 a device answer without a hashed record counts as verified -> 1 failure (verification unit).
M3 a delete applies at once without the owner's word -> 1 failure (delete is a proposal).
M4 the undo of a rename renames to the NEW name -> 1 failure (old name not back).
M5 a bare 'uygula' is a file-change confirmation with nothing pending -> 1 failure (router contract).
M6 (C#) file.write overwrites without taking the backup -> 2 failures in FileMutationTests (no backup to restore from; corrupt-backup test has no backup).
M7 (C#) file.write ignores expected_sha256 and writes over a changed file -> 1 failure (the changed file was overwritten). Restored tree rebuilt.
red_first_proof.result: 7/7 red; every file restored to its sha256 before the mutation

runtime_proof.status: PROVEN_REAL (device lab, this desktop): a real file in the lab's fixture copy was overwritten atomically, its backup written to the undo store with a hash, and file.restore brought the original bytes back (the hash read back equal to the original's); a real file was renamed, moved, copied, sent to the Recycle Bin with a backup and restored. The Cloud Core flows (journal, gate, undo, REST, Cockpit) are proven against the fake desktop whose answers are the shapes the real device's lab tests answer. The production round (a file changed through the owner's voice, its hash journaled, undone, the original back on the owner's machine) is Karar 0's (READY_FOR_OWNER).
runtime_proof.why: REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED names production; no commit is made in this run by the owner's instruction, so no production round exists yet.

owner_gates.permanent_delete_policy: READY_FOR_OWNER (checkpoint 14): no setting or tool deletes permanently; a delete is the Recycle Bin with a backup; whether a permanent delete should ever exist, and behind what confirmation, is the owner's decision - nothing waits on it.
owner_gates.karar_0: production release round: edit a text file by voice, confirm, undo, confirm the original is back.
